Nina (People Ops): Quick update: new travel & leave clarifications go live June 1. Short bullets below and a FAQ posted at https://redwood.internal/policies/travel-leave-jun2026 — please skim and ack the COC by May 25.

Sam K.: Does the new rule change per-trip limits for conferences?

Tara (Finance): Conference travel remains under the conference/offsite budget when submitted as a team cost. Individual per-trip limit ($1,500 international) applies to personal reimbursements. Attach e-tickets or vendor PDFs, screenshots of bank charges alone won't pass.

Priya (HR): Parental leave pilot details: primary caregivers = 18 weeks paid (pilot 12 months), secondary = 6 weeks paid. Enrollment opens June 1 for hires eligible after that date. Details and intake form: https://redwood.internal/forms/leave-intake

Rafael (ENG): If someone needs to travel with a partner for personal reasons during a work trip, will meals be covered?

PeopleOps-Bot: Meals for companions are not eligible by default. Exceptions (pre-approved recruiting/relocation) must be added to the expense and flagged.

Nina (People Ops): A few operational points:
- Effective date: June 1 for travel caps/receipts; parental leave enrollments start June 1.
- PTO rollover: up to 10 days carryover. Managers can approve payout for excess as a one-time exception.
- Code of Conduct: annual ack required by May 25; managers will see team completion.

Sam K.: Timeline for approvals if I submit parental leave paperwork?

Priya (HR): Aim for 8 weeks notice for planned leave. HR reviews within 5 business days after intake and coordinates with managers. For unexpected events, submit ASAP and we'll prioritize.

Tara (Finance): Reminder: upgrade charges (business class) need pre-approval; otherwise reimbursed at coach rate. Keep receipts consolidated per trip.

Nina (People Ops): We'll host a 25-min drop-in on Thursday 4pm in #all-hands for Q&A and will post a short FAQ. DM HR for edge cases (visa, adoption, relocation). Thanks everyone. :wave:
